title: Progressive typed output and tool handoff SDK playbook
content:
Purpose
This is a practical playbook for the Hosted API SDK experience around progressive (partial) typed output and tool handoffs. Goal: define a minimal, implementable contract that SDKs can implement today to reduce integration friction, improve observability, and provide predictable graceful degradation when tool endpoints or network paths fail.

Context
Teams keep asking for:
- usable partial results (so clients can show progressive UI)
- deterministic tool-call handoff semantics across networks and SDK languages
- a small set of clear failure modes + safe defaults for clients

Problem statements
1) Many apps want partial typed payloads (e.g., interim JSON chunks for stepwise form filling) but current streaming formats mix free text and structured frames and make client reconciliation hard.
2) Tool-calling protocols diverge between languages: some SDKs do optimistic local execution, others wait for server-confirmation. This produces inconsistent app behaviors and ops surprises.
3) Telemetry for partial frames is sparse (no per-frame latency/cost attribution), so debugging regressions after a rollout is hard.

Design principles
- Contract-first: typed frames should be negotiated up-front (schema id or proto hash) with explicit fallbacks.
- Incremental safety: each partial frame must be independently parseable and carry a monotonic sequence id + minimal provenance metadata.
- Minimal runtime ergonomics: SDKs get one small surface to adopt (no per-language explosion of shapes).
- Observability by default: frames emit standardized telemetry events (frame_received, frame_parsed, tool_handoff_started, tool_handoff_result).

Non-goals
- Not trying to replace existing long-lived streaming formats immediately. This is an incremental compatibility layer for SDKs and hosted API.
- Not specifying a full schema language — we accept references to external schema registries.

Recommended contract (high-level)
1) Handshake: client includes `schema_hint` in call metadata. Server responds with `schema_resolution` at stream start (success | fallback | unknown-schema).
2) Envelope: every streamed chunk is a compact envelope: [seq, type, schema_ref?, payload_snip, provenance]. `seq` monotonic, `type`: text|typed|tool-event|checkpoint, `schema_ref` is optional but present for typed frames.
3) Typed frames: payload_snip is JSON (partial or full) that must validate against the schema_ref when the schema is resolved. SDKs must expose a parse-time error path when validation fails.
4) Tool handoff token: When a model emits a tool invocation, the server emits a `tool-call` envelope with `handoff_token` (opaque, short-lived), `tool_manifest` (id + minimal metadata), and `preflight` (optional encoded prompt). SDKs call the tool backend (or forward token to user systems).
5) Acknowledgement model: tool backends must return an ack (tool_ack) with `handoff_token` and `result_ref` (or error). Server uses ack to emit a final typed result frame referencing result_ref.

Examples (developer-focused)
- Client initiates: POST /v1/streams?schema_hint=invoice.v2
- Server stream start: {seq:0,type:"checkpoint",schema_resolution:"fallback:invoice.v1"}
- Model emits partial typed: {seq:5,type:"typed",schema_ref:"invoice.v1#hash",payload_snip:{"lines":[{"desc":"par"}],"total":null}}
- Model emits tool call: {seq:6,type:"tool-event",tool:{id:"ocr.extract"},handoff_token:"tkn_3y"} -> SDK forwards to configured tool provider with token
- Tool ack: {seq:7,type:"tool-event",tool_ack:{handoff_token:"tkn_3y",status:"accepted",run_id:"r_092"}}
- Server final typed frame: {seq:8,type:"typed",schema_ref:"invoice.v1#hash",payload_snip:{"lines":[{"desc":"partial text","amount":12.5}],"total":12.5}}

SDK ergonomics (suggested surface)
1) One streaming adapter class `ProgressiveStream` (JS/Go/Python): exposes: onCheckpoint, onTypedFrame(schemaRef, frame), onTextDelta(delta), onToolEvent(tool, token), onError, close().
2) Schema resolution helper: `resolveSchema(schema_hint)` returns (resolved_ref|fallback_ref|null) and is cached per session.
3) Tool forwarding API: `forwardTool(handoff_token, tool_config)` with built-in retry policy and a single pluggable adapter for each language.
4) Validation options: SDKs must provide two modes: `strict` (throw on validation error) and `tolerate` (emit validation telemetry + best-effort parse). Default: tolerate.

Failure modes and safe defaults
- Missing schema resolution: emit checkpoint with `schema_resolution:unknown` and switch SDK to pass-through text mode for typed frames.
- Tool provider unreachable: SDK should return a standardized `tool_call_failed` event to the stream and proceed with `degraded-tool-skeleton` placeholder frame so UI can render an offline action path.
- Out-of-order frames: SDK must reorder by seq and expose a small reordering window (configurable default 250ms). Frames outside the window should raise `seq_gap` telemetry and trigger a resume fetch flow.

Telemetry & observability
Standardized events (export to console/trace/metrics):
- stream.start (schema_hint, resolved_schema, client_lang)
- frame.received (seq,type,schema_ref,size_bytes)
- frame.validated (seq,ok|fail,validation_errors_count)
- tool.handoff.start (handoff_token,tool_id)
- tool.handoff.ack (handoff_token,status,latency_ms)
- tool.handoff.fail (handoff_token,error_code)
- stream.resume.attempt (reason)

Metric KPIs to monitor on rollout
- % of streams with schema resolved at start
- mean time from tool-event to tool_ack (per tool)
- fraction of typed frames failing validation
- user-observed partial-latency (time until first typed partial frame)

Compatibility and migration path
- Phase 0 (opt-in): server emits envelopes but default SDKs ignore typed frames unless explicitly enabled by client option `enable_typed_playbook=true`.
- Phase 1 (SDK adoption): ship ProgressiveStream adapter in JS/Go/Python with `tolerate` default. SDKs will emit telemetry and attach a lightweight schema cache.
- Phase 2 (opt-out compatibility): Hosted API will require schema_hint for some latency-critical endpoints and offer an automatic fallback policy documented in SDKs.

Security and privacy considerations
- Handoff tokens must be short-lived and bound to origin+client id to prevent replay.
- Tool manifests can contain PII-sensitive preflight content; SDKs must provide redaction helpers and integrations with KMS for storing result_refs.

Operational playbook (SRE/CS)
- On tool backpressure spikes: feature-flag automatic degrade to `toolless` mode for affected customer routes and notify via console banner + incident channel.
- On schema migration (breaking change): provide a `schema_compat` endpoint that runs a dry-run validation against historical streams and surfaces top offending prompts.

Open questions (for product / research)
- Should handoff_token be single-hop opaque or verifiable JWT with limited claims? Tradeoffs: ops simplicity vs. cross-provider traceability.
- How aggressively should server speculatively prefetch tool results? (Configurable TTLs vs. deterministic execution)
- How should multi-tool transactions be represented (atomicity vs. idempotent partials)?

Acceptance criteria for initial rollout
- SDKs (JS + Python) implement ProgressiveStream and forward tool events via the adapter.
- Server emits envelope frames with seq and type for 90% of streaming routes behind a feature flag.
- Telemetry events appear in Console and map to the standard metrics above.
- Run a customer pilot with 2 users integrating invoice extraction or agent-style tool calls and measure tool_ack latency and typed-frame validation rates.

Next steps and owners
- Engineering: build the envelope encoder/decoder and SDK adapters (owner: Marco Ruiz)
- Product: finalize schema registry contract + migration checklist (owner: Aisha Patel)
- Applied ML: measure model-side partial stability when producing typed frames (owner: Yvonne Chen)
- SRE: author operational playbook and alerting rules (owner: Derek O'Neal)

Notes to reviewers
- This is intentionally prescriptive but incremental: aim for SDK primitives that are tiny and easy to adopt. Feedback sought: whether the ack-based handoff (token+ack) is sufficient for multi-party tool graphs, and whether the default `tolerate` validation mode makes sense for most customers.

Appendix: small checklist for SDK implementers
- [ ] implement seq reorder buffer with default 250ms window
- [ ] emit standardized telemetry events above
- [ ] provide forwardTool adapter with 3x retry + exponential backoff
- [ ] expose schema resolution cache and a `force_refresh` API
- [ ] surface a clear validation error callback to app owners

End of draft.
